liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (4 reviews): Reviewer says Sugaree shows the band back in top form; Calls Sugaree possibly one of the best ever, within a Jack Straw, Sugaree, Rooster opening run with the crowd getting wild [29][32][35][36]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Let It Grow closing set one is where the show really exploded; Let It Grow is described as fiendish, almost scary [29][39]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Likes the half-cocked intro leading into Estimated out of Franklin's Tower [37]
- **Space** (1 review): Calls the drums/space fun to play loud [37]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Jack Straw and Sugaree show Jerry playing fast with every note distinct [39]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd85-03-25 s1 t01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t02 Jack Straw**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t03 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t04 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t05 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t06 It's All Over Now**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t07 It Must Have Been The Roses**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]
- **gd85-03-25 s1 t08 Let It Grow**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [41]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-03-25.140842.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496** (recommended): audience recording; 21 songs; 156 min [1]
- **gd1985-03-25.150966.sbd.latvala.eaton.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [4]
- **gd1985-03-25.sbd.fix-shinid-15403.tetzeli.84410.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 3.62/5 by 13 [5]. Said about its sound: Set one was pitch-stretched about 104.6% and set two about 100.9%; uploader doubts both sets share one source [5]
- **gd85-03-25.oade-schoeps.sacks.23222.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 161 min; rated 3.75/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Recording by Jim and Doug Oade is described as very good sounding; Set one has crowd cuts between some songs in this Oade source; Disc 2/3 has an intermittent high-pitched whine or squeak during Help, Slipknot and Estimated [29][33][38]
- **gd1985-03-25.164911.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 167 min [7]
- **gd85-03-25.nak300.barbella.14497.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 158 min; rated 4.21/5 by 19 [16]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is clear and exciting, needing no effort to listen through talkers or poor equipment; Reviewer finds this audience source cleaner than the soundboard, whose first-set pitch runs far too fast; Audience recording is nice, though Jerry's vocals could be louder [31][32][34]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended, having seen about 20 Dead shows between 1981 and 1985 [35]
- Attendee describes the band as rocking, with a high-energy first set and a well-played second set with nice post-space [36]
- Attendee stood on the floor about 15 feet from Jerry and Bob in a rather small arena [37]
- Names this their favorite 1985 show [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-03-25.140842.unknown.bryant.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Robert Bryant; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Robert Bryant's Master Audience Cassettes; unknown mics > Sony TC-D5M; Transfer Info: Master Cassettes (Nakamichi CR-7A)> Tascam DA-3000 (DSF… [1]. Also: A Sennheiser 421 source supplies the tuning and first seconds of It's All Over Now, plus a 0:24 patch [1]
- **gd1985-03-25.150966.sbd.latvala.eaton.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1648**: transferred by Rob Eaton;Tim Dalton;Scott Clugston; source: Master Vault Cassettes > Dick Latvala's 1st generation cassettes > Rob Eaton's DAT (16/48) > Tim Dalton's DAT (16/48) [4]. Also: Oade Schoeps source supplies set break announcement, patches in Eyes of the World and Drums, and the final Day Job seconds [4]
- **gd1985-03-25.sbd.fix-shinid-15403.tetzeli.84410.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Pitched and patched by Bill Tetzeli; source: Original SRC: MSC>Cass.>DAT>CDR>SHN [5]
- **gd85-03-25.oade-schoeps.sacks.23222.sbeok.flacf**: taped by Oade Brothers; transferred by Doug Oade and Darrin Sacks; source: Audience - Schoeps CMC441's [6]
- **gd1985-03-25.164911.nak304.thomas.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Stephen Thomas; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Stephen Thomas' Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 300 mics + CP4 shotguns > Sony D5M [7]. Also: Master cassettes from Stephen Thomas; an AKG 451 and Neumann U87 blend supplies the first seconds of It's All Over Now [7]
- **gd85-03-25.nak300.barbella.14497.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Tommy Danscuk and Steve Barbella; source: Audience - Nak 300's [16]

claims.text: Reviewer says Sugaree shows the band back in top form
Let It Grow closing set one is where the show really exploded
Recording by Jim and Doug Oade is described as very good sounding
Audience recording is clear and exciting, needing no effort to listen through talkers or poor equipment
Reviewer finds this audience source cleaner than the soundboard, whose first-set pitch runs far too fast
Calls Sugaree possibly one of the best ever, within a Jack Straw, Sugaree, Rooster opening run with the crowd getting wild
Names this their favorite 1985 show
Set one has crowd cuts between some songs in this Oade source
Disc 2/3 has an intermittent high-pitched whine or squeak during Help, Slipknot and Estimated
Audience recording is nice, though Jerry's vocals could be louder
Attendee says the third Sugaree solo gave him and his friend the coolest moment of any show they saw
Reviewer attended, having seen about 20 Dead shows between 1981 and 1985
Attendee found the Sugaree outstanding
Attendee describes the band as rocking, with a high-energy first set and a well-played second set with nice post-space
Attendee stood on the floor about 15 feet from Jerry and Bob in a rather small arena
Likes the half-cocked intro leading into Estimated out of Franklin's Tower
Calls the drums/space fun to play loud
Notes high-frequency squeaking during Help>Slipknot and Estimated, wondering if it is a bleeding metronome
Jack Straw and Sugaree show Jerry playing fast with every note distinct
Let It Grow is described as fiendish, almost scary
Master audience cassette from Robert Bryant, transferred by Charlie Miller
A Sennheiser 421 source supplies the tuning and first seconds of It's All Over Now, plus a 0:24 patch
Soundboard from Dick Latvala's vault cassettes; Rob Eaton's first-generation cassette went to DAT via Tim Dalton, coordinated by Charlie Miller
Oade Schoeps source supplies set break announcement, patches in Eyes of the World and Drums, and the final Day Job seconds
Set one was pitch-stretched about 104.6% and set two about 100.9%; uploader doubts both sets share one source
Master cassettes from Stephen Thomas; an AKG 451 and Neumann U87 blend supplies the first seconds of It's All Over Now
